title: Guitar 4-Week
subtitle: Clean chords, natural groove & fretboard freedom

cards.hint: Keep fingers 2 & 3 glued together and drop one string set
cards.back: Em: 0-2-2-0-0-0  →  Am: x-0-2-2-1-0 (drop pair from A/D to D/G, add index on B1).
cards.example: 2-min drill: Set 60 BPM. Strum on beat 1, float shapes cleanly on beats 2-3-4. Keep fingertips right behind the fret wire.

cards.front: G → Cadd9 → Dsus4 with 2 locked anchor fingers
cards.hint: Ring finger on B3, pinky on high e3 NEVER lift!
cards.example: Unlocks hundreds of acoustic songs in Week 1 because your ring and pinky stay planted like a compass pivot.

cards.front: A string buzzes or sounds muted inside an open C (x-3-2-0-1-0). What's the 3-point fix?
cards.back: 1) Drop thumb to the middle-back of the neck, 2) Push wrist slightly forward so fingertips land vertically, 3) Slide right behind each fret.
cards.example: Arpeggiate strings one by one (A→D→G→B→e) to spot and celebrate every clear ringing note.

cards.front: The Universal 'Island / Folk' Strum in 4/4 time
cards.back: D  -  D  U  -  U  D  U   (miss the strings on beat 3 downstroke, keep the pendulum swinging).
cards.example: Secret to effortless rhythm: your wrist is a continuous metronome; you simply choose which passes brush the strings.

cards.front: How do you make a 3-chord song sound like a studio recording?
cards.back: Brush only the low bass strings on beat 1, then accent the bright top strings on beats 2 and 4.
cards.example: Add light palm muting (edge of picking palm resting on the bridge saddles) in the verse, then lift open for the chorus.

cards.front: Play the I – V – vi – IV progression in the key of G
cards.back: G  →  D  →  Em  →  C   (4 beats each, loop smoothly).
cards.example: Pop a capo on fret 2 and the exact same shapes sound in the bright key of A major.

cards.hint: Thumb owns low 3 strings; index=G, middle=B, ring=e
cards.back: Thumb alternates steady quarter notes (Bass-D-Bass-D) while index & middle pluck B and G in between: P - i - P - m.
cards.example: Loop slowly over C and Am with rainy ambient audio—one of the most meditative sounds on earth.

cards.hint: One finger per fret from fret 5 to fret 8
cards.example: Sing a tiny 3-note phrase, then find it inside the box—leave breathing space between phrases just like speech.

cards.front: Name the natural notes on the Low E string without hesitating
cards.hint: Every pair is 2 frets apart EXCEPT E–F and B–C (1 fret!)
cards.example: Knowing the low E string automatically names every root-6 power chord, barre chord, and pentatonic key.

cards.front: Effortless F Barre Chord (1-3-3-2-1-1) without hand cramps
cards.hint: Don't clamp with your thumb — use arm leverage and the bony side of your index
cards.back: Roll index finger 15° onto its firm thumb-side edge, pull gently back with your right forearm against the guitar body, relax thumb.
cards.example: Warm-up stepping stone: Fmaj7 (x-3-3-2-1-0) gives lush, dreamy color with zero barre fatigue.

cards.front: Hammer-ons & Pull-offs inside open chords (folk embellishment)
cards.hint: Snap down briskly; flick slightly downward on release
cards.back: Strum Am (x-0-2-2-1-0), lift index to Asus2 (B0), then hammer briskly back onto B1 in rhythm.
cards.example: Also magical on D (hammer middle onto e2) and C (hammer middle onto D2).

cards.front: Major vs. Minor vs. Dominant 7th — hear the emotional color instantly
cards.back: Major = bright & resolved · Minor = introspective & warm · Dominant 7th = bluesy tension asking to resolve home (A7 → D).
cards.example: Close your eyes, strum slowly, feel the resonance in your chest—calm mind, musical ear.
